answer: A copper split-tally bond: each identity holds a copper half, the registry the other, matched by a shared cipher. Agents file quill-signed claims with their halves; the registry recomputes the cipher and rejects reused halves. Minting: 45 credits, so one fake is 45+30=75, k-th 75+10(k-1); 1,000 fakes: 5,070,000 vs 40,000 pool. Borrowed halves fail: claims need the owner's quill signature. Honest agents pay 45 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
